strengths: The joint focus on clean generalization, robust training accuracy, and robust test error addresses an important phenomenon that robustness guarantees alone do not explain.

The proposed signal-learning and noise-memorization decomposition offers an interpretable hypothesis for CGRO. Connecting this hypothesis to representation complexity and training dynamics is potentially useful.
Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and synthetic data provide descriptive evidence, with additional input-loss flatness diagnostics in the appendix.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider a balanced distribution on x = ±e1 with corresponding labels, radius δ = 0.2, and f_clean(x) = x_1 − 0.9. This satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3: clean error is zero and robust error is 1/2. With N = D samples, both atoms occur with substantial empirical frequency with high probability, so vanishing robust training error forces zero robust population error; a CGRO classifier cannot exist. Additional conditions controlling support coverage are necessary.

The representation proof has further substantive gaps. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes only, whereas Lemma 4.5 incorrectly concludes that all training perturbation balls are disjoint; the subsequent algebraic rewriting therefore need not hold. Appendix F also claims uniformly vanishing approximation error for a generally discontinuous indicator-based function using continuous ReLU networks. Softening the indicators cannot establish this uniform claim, and no boundary-mass or classification-margin argument supplies an alternative.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish robustness under the stated threat model. Training attacks modify only the meaningful patch along w*, leaving every noise patch untouched, whereas Definition 3.3 measures robust training error over the entire norm ball. Small loss against the restricted attack does not imply small unrestricted robust training error. The proof explicitly makes this unsupported implication, undermining the claimed CGRO guarantee.

Essential steps in the training-dynamics proof are invalid. The clean-test analysis on page 25 treats cubic Gaussian noise as sub-Gaussian, although even a single nonzero Gaussian cube does not have sub-Gaussian tails. Furthermore, Hypothesis E.1 requires initial signal components to be at most Õ(α^−1), but Assumption 5.7 permits c_α > 1/2 while initialization has standard deviation polylog(d)/√d. Thus the induction base is not guaranteed throughout the claimed parameter regime. These issues require substantial proof and assumption revisions.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is also false as stated. A constant classifier has zero input-loss gradient, making the proposed correction term zero. Nevertheless, with label-dependent logistic loss, empirical and population risks differ through random class proportions, and population risk exceeds empirical risk with nonvanishing probability. Smooth input densities do not eliminate this sampling fluctuation.

The experiments do not convincingly validate the theoretical mechanisms. Section 6.2 sets δ = α = 10, contradicting the theorem's strict δ < α condition and permitting complete removal of the meaningful signal. It therefore does not test the claimed robustly separable regime. The image capacity sweeps also do not distinguish representation limitations from optimization failure, particularly when smaller MNIST models remain at chance. Missing attack settings, optimization details, synthetic test-set size, and repeated-run uncertainty limit reproduction and assessment.

The originality of Theorem 4.7 needs clarification. As the manuscript describes Li et al. (2022), an existential hard distribution admitting a linear clean classifier already satisfies the broader polynomial-size ReLU assumption. Enlarging the admissible distribution class therefore does not itself strengthen that existential lower bound. The potentially distinctive contributions are the CGRO construction and learning dynamics, but their central guarantees are not supported by sound proofs in the present manuscript.
